chunks: They are wrong who liken Thee

and dress Thee with apparel of the creatures by their imagination, attribute to Thee parts of body by their own thinking and consider Thee after the creatures of various types, through the working of their intelligence.

key_terms.الْعَادِلُونَ: those who equate or liken (God to creatures)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe the error of anthropomorphism in understanding God's nature?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Al-Ashbaah*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the anthropomorphizers (*al-Mujassima*) who project their limited, composite intellects onto the Divine, thereby reducing the Absolute to a created entity with distinct parts and varying powers. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on *Tawhid al-Jawhari* (Unity of Essence), distinguishing between God's transcendence and the finite nature of human perception. The critique underscores that attributing physical form or multiplicity to God is a falsehood born of imaginative projection rather than rational insight.

en.sayed-ali-raza: They are wrong who liken Thee

to their idols, and dress Thee with apparel of the creatures by their imagination, attribute to Thee parts of body by their own thinking and consider Thee after the creatures of various types, through the working of their intelligence.
